questions.question: In which of the following years did Japan invade India resulting in the Battle of Imphal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1944**__.

__
 
• **In 1944,**____** Japan invade India resulting in the Battle of Imphal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Battle of Imphal** took place from March to July 1944 in the vicinity of the city of Imphal, the capital of the state of Manipur in northeastern India.

 
 
• Japanese forces attempted to destroy the Allied forces at Imphal and invade India, but were driven back to Burma with heavy losses.
 
• Together with the Battle of Kohima on the road, by which the Allied forces at Imphal were relieved, the battle was the turning point of the Burma Campaign, which was part of the South-East Asian Theater of World War II.
 
• The defeats at Kohima and Imphal were the largest defeats to date in Japanese history, with many Japanese deaths from hunger, disease and exhaustion during their retreat.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The operation to take** Imphal** was named **U-go** by the **Japanese Army.**
 
• It consisted of elements from the **31st Infantry Division** of the **Japanese Army **and as well as units from the I**ndian National Army,** who were in primarily support and scouting roles.
 
• The **Japanese Army** crossed into **India** on the night of** 7th March** and engaged the **British Indian forces** guarding the frontiers the morning of **8th March 1944.**

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Magnetic flux is a vector quantity.
Two magnetic field lines may intersect.
The net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero.
Earth's magnetic poles coincide with the geographic poles.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The net magnetic flux through any closed surface will be zero__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Gauss' Law for Magnetism:**

 
 
• Gauss' Law for magnetism applies to the magnetic flux through a closed surface. In this case, the area vector points out from the surface.
 
• Because magnetic field lines are continuous loops, all closed surfaces have as many magnetic field lines going in as coming out. Hence, the net magnetic flux through a closed surface is zero.
 
• Net flux = ∫ B • dA = 0
 
• Gauss' Law for charges was a very useful method for calculating electric fields in highly symmetric situations.
 
• Gauss' Law for magnetism is considerably less useful, but we'll come up with another law that enables us to calculate magnetic fields in highly symmetric situations. 
 
 

Magnetic flux:

 
• Magnetic flux is defined as the number of magnetic field lines passing through a given closed surface.
 
• It provides the measurement of the total magnetic field that passes through a given surface area.
 
• It is a scalar quantity.
 
• The SI unit of magnetic flux is Weber (Wb).

​Magnetic flux associated with any area is given as,

⇒ ϕB = BAcosθ

Where ϕB = magnetic flux, B = magnetic field intensity, A = area, and θ = angle between B and A

questions.question: Plants grown at which of the following places take up carbon dioxide during the night?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Desert**__.

__
 
• **Plants grown in Desert places take up carbon dioxide during the night**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** desert plants** which grow in **semi-arid conditions **fix atmospheric** CO₂** to form **malic acid** in the **dark**.

 
 
• These plants accumulate **organic acid** intermediate during the **night** to be used during the **daytime**.
 
• This pathway is called **Crassulacean acid metabolism** (CAM) and the plants which carry out crassulacean metabolism are termed **CAM plants**. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Different Parts of a Plant: A detailed description of each of the parts of plants is mentioned below:**

 
 
• **Roots**: Roots are the most important part of a plant as they are responsible for transferring the necessary nutrients to the plant. They are the agents responsible for delivering water and minerals to the plants. 
 
• **Stems**: Stems are also support systems for the plants. Their main function is to act as delivery agents for the nutrients and water stored in the roots and transfer them to the other plant parts in the form of glucose.
 
• **Leaves**: Leaves are a fundamental part of a plant as all the necessary food for the plants are stored in the leaves. 
 
• **Flowers**: Flowers are known as the reproductive products of plants. They are mostly responsible for producing fruits.
 
• **Fruits**: Fruits are the products of reproduction in plants. The most essential component from which reproduction starts, that is the seed, is present in the fruit.
 
• **Seeds**: Seeds are the main agents for reproduction. They can be found most commonly in fruits from where they germinate and develop into new plants.

questions.question: Which of the following is **NOT **a storage root?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Breathing root**__.

__
 
• **A breathing root is NOT a storage root**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Breathing roots** are **respiratory roots** found in** halophytes** such as **mangroves**.

 
 
• They often grow in** saline swamps**, so breathing roots come out of the **water **to **consume oxygen**.
 
• **Pneumatophores**, commonly found in **mangrove species** that grow in **saline mudflats**, are lateral **roots that grow upward out **of the** mud** and **water **to function as the site of** oxygen intake** for the submerged primary **root system**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Root **
 **Details**
 
 

 **Napiform root**
 
 
 
• Napiform roots are the modifications of taproot which become swollen and spherical at the upper end while their lower end is tapered like a thread.
 
• Some examples of napiform roots are- turnip (Brassica rapa), sugar beet.
 
 
 
 

 **Conical root**
 
 
 
• This type of root tuber is conical in shape.
 
• In the conical form of root modification, the roots are swollen and are broad at the base, the apex part gradually tapers forming a con-like structure like in a carrot.
 
 
 
 

 **Fusiform root**
 
 
 
• The fusiform root is the modification of taproot for food storage.
 
• The fusiform root is swollen in the middle and tapering towards both ends forming a spindle-shaped structure. e.g. Radish (Raphanus sativus).

questions.question: The main collections of Vedic hymns are called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Samhita**__.

__
 
• **The main collections of Vedic hymns are called Samhita**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Rigveda Samhita** is the oldest extant Indic text.

 
 
• It is a collection of **1,028 Vedic Sanskrit hymns** and **10,600 verses** in all, organized into **ten books** (Sanskrit: mandalas).
 
• The **hymns** are dedicated to **Rigvedic deities**. 
 
 
 
• **Samhitas** are **ritualistic texts**, and they explain the social and religious importance of** rituals**.
 
 
• Each **Samhita** has added texts called Brahmanas, which have commentaries on the hymns and rituals.
 
• Each** brahmana** has an** Aranyaka** (forest text) and an **Upanishad**.
 
• The **Aranyakas** contain mystical ritual instructions to be undertaken in secret by the sages who live in the **forests.**
 
• **Upanishads** deal with philosophical inquiries.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sutra:**

 
 
• ​Sutra in Indian literary traditions refers to an aphorism or a collection of aphorisms in the form of a manual or, more broadly, a condensed manual or text.
 
• Sutras are a genre of ancient and medieval Indian texts found in Hinduism, Buddhism and Jainism. 
 
 
 
• **Pad**:
 
 
• Pad refers to a **word or foot** in the context of Vedic texts. In particular, each verse (Rik) of a hymn can be broken down into multiple padas (feet).
 
 
 
• ​**Mukh**:
 
 
• Mukh means **face or mouth** in Sanskrit.

questions.question: Siddhendra Yogi, a doyen of the ______ dance form, was lauded as Adi Guru.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuchipudi**__.

__
 
• **Siddhendra Yogi, a doyen of the Kuchipudi dance form, was lauded as Adi Guru**__.

 __
 
• ​**K****uchipudi,** one of eight** classical dance** styles of **India.**
 
• **Kuchipudi **is indigenous to the state of** Andhra Pradesh** and differs from the other** five classical styles** by the inclusion of **singing**.
 
• **Kuchipudi** is a dance-drama performance art that originated in a **village** of** Krishna district **of **Andhra Pradesh, India.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Siddhendra Yogi **was an exceptional scholar and artist of the 14th century AD.

 
 
• The dance form of Kuchipudi saw a revolution during the Bhakti movement between the 11th and 13th centuries.
 
• Siddhendra Yogi covers the principles of dance of Natya Shastra, the Bible of all Indian classical dance styles.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Dance**
 **Details**
 
 

 **Bharatanatyam**
 
 
 
• Bharatanatyam is a major form of Indian classical dance that originated in the modern-day region of Tamil Nadu.
 
• Bharatanatyam is the state dance form of Tamil Nadu.
 
 
 
 

 **Kathakali**
 
 
 
• Kathakali is a major form of classical Indian dance.
 
• It is a "story play" genre of art, but one distinguished by the elaborately colorful make-up, costumes and face masks that the traditionally male actor-dancers wear.
 
 
 
 

 **Kathak**
 
 
 
• Kathak is one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance.
 
• Kathak performances include Urdu Ghazals and commonly used instruments brought during the Mughal period.

questions.question: Chandragupta Maurya led a revolt against the ______ and overthrew them.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nandas**__.

__
 
• **Chandragupta Maurya**__ __**led a revolt against the Nandas and overthrew them**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **4th century B.C**., **Nanda kings** ruled the **Magadha dynasty** and this dynasty was the most **powerful kingdom** of the **north.**

 
 
• A Brahman minister called** Chanakya** also known as **Kautilya** trained a young man i.e.**Chandragupta Maurya.**
 
• **Chandragupta** organized his **own army **and overthrew the** Nanda king Dhana Nand** in **322 B.C**.In the** 4th century B.C.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chandragupta Maurya:**

 
 
• He was the architect of the Maurya Empire which controlled the plains of both the Indus and the Ganges, and which extended to the eastern and western oceans.
 
• He laid the foundation for an extensive and efficient system of centralized administration and tax-collection which formed the basis of his empire.
 
• Trade and agriculture were reformed and regulated, with the creation of infrastructure and standardization of weights and measures, and provisions were made for a large standing army.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
 

 Dynasty
 Details
 
 

 Shishunagas
 
 
 
• The Shaishunaga dynasty is believed to have been the second ruling dynasty of Magadha in ancient India.
 
• It was succeeded by the Nanda Empire, which became one of the most powerful dynasties in the region.
 
 
 
 

 Kushanas
 
 
 
• The Kushan Empire was a syncretic empire, formed by the Yuezhi, in the Bactrian territories in the early 1st century.
 
• The Kushans possibly used the Greek language initially for administrative purposes, but soon began to use the Bactrian language.
 
 
 
 

 Haryankas
 
 
 
• The Haryanka dynasty was the first ruling dynasty of Magadha, an empire of ancient India. Initially, the capital was Rajagriha.

questions.question: ______ is the external agency applied on a body to change its state of rest or uniform motion.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Force**__.

__
 
• **Force is the external agency applied on a body to change its state of rest or uniform motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton's first law of motion:**

 
 
• Newton's first law states that if a body is at rest or moving at a constant speed in a straight line, it will remain at rest or keep moving in a straight line at constant speed unless it is acted upon by a force.
 
 
• This postulate is known as the law of inertia.
 
 
 
• The law of inertia was first formulated by Galileo Galilei for horizontal motion on Earth and was later generalized by René Descartes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In thermodynamics, **heat** is energy in transfer to or from a thermodynamic system, by mechanisms other than thermodynamic work or transfer of matter.
 
• **Power **is defined as the rate of doing work.
 
 
• It is the ratio of work done (W) and time taken (t).
 
• The SI unit of power is the watt (W), in honor of the physicist James Watt.
 
 
 
• In physics, **energy** is the quantitative property that must be transferred to a body or physical system to perform work on the body, or to heat it.
